text: DSH Git 是面向 DSH Web 与桌面宿主的 Git 插件，在会话输入区提供分支入口，并把变更、差异和提交图放入右侧栏。它通过宿主 subprocess 服务调用 Git，展示仓库状态、分支、暂存与未暂存文件，支持差异查看、提交、推送和分支切换。还可管理工作树，并连接 GitHub 或配置的 GitLab 浏览远程项目。适合在 DSH 会话中查看和操作当前代码仓库；提交信息建议生成可选，需宿主提供可用模型。

DSH Git adds repository tools to DSH Web and desktop. Its right sidebar shows status, branches, file changes, diffs, and history. Users can stage, commit, push, switch branches, and manage worktrees. Optional GitHub and GitLab views show remote projects; commit message suggestions use the model.
想在 DSH 里查看当前会话目录对应的 Git 状态和分支。
能不能在聊天界面旁边暂存文件并提交代码？
我想从侧边栏逐个查看暂存和工作区文件的差异。
让 DSH 能为不同会话显示各自仓库的变更。
需要在一个项目里新建独立工作树来处理另一项任务。
Git 分支怎么在 DSH 会话里快速切换？
I want to review staged and unstaged file diffs inside DSH.
Can DSH show my repository history and help me manage branches?
DSH Git 的功能「仓库状态与变更列表」：按会话目录发现 Git 仓库，并显示当前分支、HEAD、暂存、未暂存及未跟踪文件。用户从会话中的 Git 入口打开变更视图。
DSH Git 的功能「差异查看与暂存提交」：用户可查看单个文件的工作区或暂存区差异，切换暂存状态并提交变更；差异文件可从侧栏打开。
DSH Git 的功能「工作树管理」：在宿主工作树运行时可用时，或启用本地实现后，创建并进入新的分支工作树，便于在同一仓库并行处理任务。
DSH Git 的功能「提交信息建议」：用户可请求模型根据暂存差异生成可编辑的提交信息建议；插件把建议填入输入框，不会代替用户提交。
DSH Git 使用前须知：Client 界面依赖宿主提供右侧栏服务；提交信息生成还需要宿主 LLM 与可解析的模型选择。
DSH Git 使用前须知：GitHub 远程功能连接 api.github.com；GitLab 远程功能需先配置实例，默认实例地址为 gitlab.com。

@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · Summary：Standard DSH/Cordis Git plugin with one portable Host service, one Client bundle, and optional Desktop enhancement. The package runs unchanged in DeepSeek Harness Desktop and in a standard DSH Web host; the npm scope `@dsh-electron/` identifies the publisher, not a runtime requirement.

@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · Summary：**Requires the upstream right sidebar.** Supported DSH releases are listed in the [compatibility contract](docs/reference/dsh-compatibility.md); their Client UI ships the right sidebar (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar-right`). Git registers three sidebar tab types through the standard two-stage path and navigates through `ctx.sidebarRight`; without the right sidebar the Client half cannot load. The third-party Details Host plugin is deprecated and no longer depended on. See the [DSH compatibility contract](docs/reference/dsh-compatibility.md) for the verified release list.

@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · Summary：[DeepSeek Harness Desktop](https://github.com/cherrchen/deepseek-harness-electron) pre-installs this plugin and mirrors this repository with git subtree. Users may disable Git from the Plugins settings; the right sidebar is an upstream built-in.

@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · DSH compatibility：See the [compatibility contract](docs/reference/dsh-compatibility.md) for the exact verified releases, development pin, host Node requirements, and candidate upgrade process.

@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · Installation：The package is published to npm as `@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git` (current `0.2.9`, MIT, with build provenance). It is still experimental development: the API and versioning remain pre-1.0 and may change between minor releases.

**DeepSeek Harness Desktop** — Git is pre-installed and enabled by default. Disable it from **Settings → Plugins** when you do not need repository UI.

@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · Installation：**DSH Web** — every supported release ships the right sidebar, so Git alone is enough. The shortest path is two commands:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git
dsh --profile web
```

`dsh plugin` forwards to pnpm inside the profile directory: it installs the package and activates the bundled `cordis.patch.yml` layer that mounts the plugin. Four install sources are supported, shown here with the `web` profile:

@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · Installation：| Source | Command | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| npm registry (recommended) | `dsh plugin --profile web add @dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git` | Prebuilt artifact; no build authorization |
| tarball | `dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-electron-dsh-plugin-git-<version>.tgz` | Prebuilt offline package; no build authorization |
| local path | `dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-plugin-git` | pnpm links the checkout; for development |
| GitHub / git | `dsh plugin --profile web add github:cherrchen/dsh-plugin-git` | Fetches sources and builds them on install through `prepare`; needs `allowBuilds`, pin a tag |

@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · Installation：Whichever source you use, the Git client requires the host to already provide the `ctx.sidebarRight` and `ctx.sidebarRightTabs` services at load time; every supported DeepSeek Harness release provides them.

@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · From the npm registry (recommended)：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git
```

The registry holds the prebuilt artifact, so no package code runs on your machine at install time.

@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · From a tarball：```sh
pnpm pack --pack-destination dist
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dist/dsh-electron-dsh-plugin-git-0.2.9.tgz
```

`pnpm pack` produces that single tarball, and every tag's GitHub Release carries the same one — for `0.2.9`, `https://github.com/cherrchen/dsh-plugin-git/releases/download/v0.2.9/dsh-electron-dsh-plugin-git-0.2.9.tgz`. It is prebuilt as well, which makes it the form to use for an offline or air-gapped profile.

@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · From GitHub：A git install fetches **sources, not built artifacts**, so the package's own `prepare` script builds the published entry points on your machine: `pnpm run build` emits the declarations with `tsc` and then bundles both faces with `tsdown`, using only this package's standalone tsconfigs, so no sibling checkout is assumed. pnpm ≥ 10 refuses to run that script until it is explicitly allowed, so the first `add` fails with `ERR_PNPM_GIT_DEP_PREPARE_NOT_ALLOWED`. Copy the exact key pnpm prints into the profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml` — for a git-hosted dependency that key is the package name plus the resolved git spec and commit, and a bare package name does not match it:

@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · From GitHub：```yaml
allowBuilds:
  # the key pnpm printed
  '@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git@git+<host>/<path>#<commit>': true
```

then run the `add` again. Moving the pin moves the commit, so the key moves with it. Treat that allowance as **permission for the package to execute code on your machine at install time**, outside any sandbox the agent runs under. Pin a tag so a later push cannot silently change what runs:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:cherrchen/dsh-plugin-git#v0.2.9
```

@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · From a local checkout (development)：```sh git clone https://github.com/cherrchen/dsh-plugin-git.git cd dsh-plugin-git pnpm install pnpm build # writes lib/, which Git ignores but the install reads pnpm links the checkout, so a later `pnpm build` is picked up without reinstalling. > **Note**: if your DSH is a source checkout rather than a global install, `dsh` is not on `PATH` — replace `dsh` with `pnpm dsh` in every command above, for example `pnpm dsh plugin --profile web add …`.

section: Pairing with the upstream right sidebar

text: @dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · Pairing with the upstream right sidebar：**Stage one** — `ctx.sidebarRightTabs.register(definition)` registers three tab types: `git.changes` and `git.graph` are page types (opened by kind, one tab per pane) that each contribute one guide entry (Changes `order: 11`, Graph `order: 12`), replacing the old Details launcher cards on the guide page; `git.diff` is a resource type with pattern `dsh-resource://git/diff/**`, a `canOpen` that validates the address decodes, and a title taken from the decoded file name. Optional Worktrees and Remote entries use orders 13 and 14, keeping all Git entries between Workspace files (10) and New terminal (20). Graph uses commit-lane artwork; Remote uses a cloud with upload/download arrows.

@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · Pairing with the upstream right sidebar：**Stage two** — each type's body component injects the `sidebar.right.pane.tab` seat under the definition's `id`; bodies read `{ address, params, revision }` from `useTabInfo().tab.navigation`.

Unified navigation converges on `ctx.sidebarRight`:

```text
ctx.sidebarRight.openTab('git.changes')
ctx.sidebarRight.openResource('dsh-resource://git/diff/<encodeURIComponent(path)>/<staged|worktree>', { params: { path, staged } })
ctx.sidebarRight.openTab('git.graph')
```

text: @dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · Pairing with the upstream right sidebar：A diff tab's identity is its exact address: re-opening the same file and comparison side reveals the existing tab and bumps its `revision` (the body refetches on it), while a staged and a working-tree diff of one file are two addresses and sit side by side. Changes and Graph dedupe per pane by kind, owned by the sidebar. The changed-files indicator, the branch chip, and the guide entries open `git.changes`; clicking a file row opens the `git.diff` for that path.

text: @dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · User experience：In the conversation composer, Git contributes a branch selector and a changed-files indicator on the left of the input area. Clicking either control opens `git.changes` as a right-sidebar tab. Creating a branch opens a shared conversation Modal; after `git init` with no commits (unborn HEAD), the menu shows the symbolic default branch as disabled, explains that the first commit is required, and disables create until HEAD exists.

@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · User experience：The selector follows that session's effective directory. Hosts that publish a `workingDirectory` session projection use it; otherwise Git keeps the session header directory. Each session has its own repository state. A linked checkout shows a worktree label. The Changes surface lists the repository's other checkouts. **Use in this session** appears only when the host can change that session's directory, and it asks the host working-directory service to enter the selected checkout; a **Manage worktrees** action opens the dedicated Worktrees tab while that tab is enabled. This package does not delete or prune worktrees.

@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · User experience：The **Changes** surface shows the current branch beside refresh, then a single-line auto-growing commit message field with a wand **Generate** control and a split **Commit** button (Commit, Amend, Commit & Push, Commit & Sync). Staged, unstaged, and untracked paths follow as icon-action sections: plus or minus toggles the index, undo discards after a two-step confirm, and a porcelain letter badges the row. Clicking a path opens the matching diff. The **Diff** adapter shows refresh in the top-right and supplies one file's working-tree or staged comparison to the official DSH `DiffBlock`, which owns copying, folding, and line wrapping where supported. Git patch conversion and non-text states are described in the [architecture overview](docs/architecture/overview.md); the original resource addresses remain restorable. The **Graph** surface shows Auto / All / First parent beside refresh, then the commit history as a canvas-drawn lane graph — one continuous coordinate space, so rails and merge edges never break at row boundaries — each commit a single line of subject, author, and kind-colored HEAD/branch/remote/tag ref chips, with a

@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · Composition：The Host plugin requires `ctx.subprocess`, provides `ctx.git`, and starts Git with an executable plus separate argv values. It never invokes a shell. When a DSH Web Host is present, an optional Connection child registers the loopback `/git` RPC channel.

@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · Composition：The Client plugin requires Connection, locale, renderer, conversation UI, primitives, session UI, and the upstream right sidebar (`ctx.sidebarRight` / `ctx.sidebarRightTabs`, type-only imports). Business components receive the controller for their session and `openDetails()` through slot injection and do not access Cordis context. Two sessions do not share one repository snapshot.

@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · Composition：When `ctx.settingsScope` or `ctx.configForms` is present, the Client registers the commit-message and worktrees configuration sections through [`src/compat/dsh-client-settings.ts`](src/compat/dsh-client-settings.ts). `0.1.5-rc.2` and `0.1.6-alpha.1` consume `settings.plugin.item` under the `git-commit-message` and `git-worktrees` namespaces, on **Settings → Plugins → Plugin configuration**. From `0.1.6-alpha.2`, hosts consume `plugins.bundle.config` with a single card keyed by package name `@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git`, on that bundle's detail page between its description and its rows. From 0.1.7 the form data is the patch row id `dsh-plugin-git`, not the package name. The configuration is absent when the host declares neither slot or does not serve that namespace.

@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · Configuration：| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| `executable` | `git` | Git executable name or absolute path resolved by `ctx.subprocess`. |
| `maxOutputBytes` | 8 MiB | Per-stream collection cap for one Git command. |
| `graceMs` | 3000 | Managed subprocess termination grace period. |
| `commitMessage.provider` | — | Provider route registered with the DSH LLM runtime. Required when `commitMessage.mode` is `custom`. |
| `commitMessage.model` | — | Model id resolved by the provider route. Required when `commitMessage.mode` is `custom`. |
| `commitMessage.mode` | inherit | `inherit` uses the host session model; `custom` pins `provider`/`model`. |
| `commitMessage.systemPrompt` | built-in | System prompt for commit-message generation. Empty/absent uses the package default. |
| `commitMessage.maxDiffBytes` | 48 KiB | Staged-diff byte cap applied before the generation prompt is built (validated minimum 1024). |
| `worktrees.enabled` | — | Follow the host's upstream `worktrees` runtime by default; set `true` to enable the local implementation when none is mounted. |
| `worktrees.directory` | `.agents/worktrees` | Checkout pool for locally

@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · Configuration：The whole `commitMessage` section is optional and is also the `git-commit-message` settings namespace; likewise `worktrees` is the `git-worktrees` settings namespace. Edit either from the plugin configuration entry above, or as a composition entry. When the host exposes no LLM runtime, or no session model and no custom route resolve, commit message generation is unavailable and the Client reports `git/generation-unavailable`.

@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · Git operations：The first release supports repository discovery, Git version, current branch and HEAD, staged/unstaged/untracked status, local branches, working and staged diffs, stage/unstage, commit, amend, push to `origin`, rebase-then-push sync, branch creation, and branch switching. Status uses porcelain v2 with NUL path separators; branches use `for-each-ref`; every caller-supplied path, branch, and message remains one argv value. Status also records whether the checkout is the main worktree, a linked worktree, or bare, and lists checkouts with `git worktree list --porcelain`. Entering another checkout changes that session's directory through the host working-directory service and only accepts a path from that list. Creating a checkout goes through the host's experimental `worktrees` runtime when mounted — which also enters the new checkout — or through this plugin's own `git worktree add -b` when the `git-worktrees` `enabled` setting is on; deleting and pruning worktrees stay outside this package.

@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · Git operations：Discard restores one staged, unstaged, or untracked change, including an addition or rename edited after staging, through explicit index, worktree, and clean operations. It is destructive: the Client always asks for a second, explicit confirmation before sending the RPC, and the surface names the path in the confirm body.

@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · Git operations：Commit history is read with a paged `git log` (`GIT_LOG_FORMAT`, one commit per line, fixed field count) so the Graph surface appends older commits incrementally through a scroll sentinel instead of materializing the whole history.

@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · Git operations：Commit message generation is opt-in at the host: it needs an LLM runtime and a resolvable model (the session default, or a custom `provider`/`model`). A staged diff (capped by `commitMessage.maxDiffBytes`) is sent to that route and the streamed suggestion is written into the editable commit message input. The system prompt defaults to a Conventional Commit instruction and can be overridden from Plugin configuration. Generation is suggestion-only — it never stages, commits, or pushes anything.

@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · Git operations：GitHub Remote is available when the host provides the complete optional credentials seam: authentication, PR/Issue browsing, comparisons, PR comments/reviews, verified checkout, Issue branches, and guarded create/close/merge. See the [remote RPC contract](docs/reference/remote-platform-rpc.en.md) for configuration, limits, credential handling and unknown-result recovery, and the [active plan](docs/plans/active/remote-platform-integration.en.md) for acceptance evidence and unverified external scenarios. Git fetch/push uses existing Git transport credentials, independently of platform login. Stash, cherry-pick and merge-conflict editing remain outside this package.

@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · Model Experience：None, as this package registers no model tools, prompt sections, or request context.
@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · KV Cache effect：None. Commit-message generation is an independent Host LLM request and does not add, replace, or retain session tokens.

@dsh-electron/dsh-plugin-git README · Known Limitations and Deferred Work：- **Independent Git transport** — Remote platform login does not configure Git fetch/push credentials; existing helpers or SSH remain responsible for Git authentication.
- **Bounded command output** — a diff larger than `maxOutputBytes` retains only the subprocess collector's tail, so deployments handling very large diffs must raise that validated setting.
- **Generation needs host + model** — commit message generation requires a host LLM runtime and a resolvable model (session default or a custom route in Plugin configuration); without either, the Generate action stays disabled or reports `git/generation-unavailable`.
- **Worktree entry needs a live directory service** — without the host working-directory service, or without a live agent for that session, the checkout list stays read-only. Writes then keep the previous caller-supplied repository contract. A missing directory is not repaired here; recovery belongs to the host working-directory service.
- **Worktree creation needs a reported mode** — the Worktrees tab appears only while the host reports `upstream` (the experimental `worktrees` service is mount
